note: Fixed passive-follow bug: _sanitize_name stripped '.' instead of replacing with '_', so every '.001'-suffixed glTF node (both chrome pistons + several hose morph meshes) failed _find_path resolution and were silently dropped from the passive rig. Cylinder pivots rotated but pistons/hoses stayed frozen -> 'cylinder/ferrule follow broken during tilt'. Verified bake data against AnimationPlayer ground truth (exact match at ±45°). Changes: _sanitize_name -> validate_node_name(); _apply_pose drives absolute axis-angle (clip semantics; rest was identity anyway); test now asserts 4 passive nodes + piston position follows. attachment_switch_test + model_switch/bucket_soil_tool/excavation_gameplay all pass.

Root-caused remaining tilt-follow defects: (1) _axis_from_name('z') returned Vector3.FORWARD (-z) while the baked table keys angles to the +z quaternion component — joint twist was always mirrored against passive samples: pistons extended on the wrong side, rod ends detached from the bracket, cylinders counter-rotated. (2) bake script read morph-weight channels as a single scalar — glTF stores weights flat (keys x 18 targets); hoses got 1 bogus weight on TILT_M45 only, collapsing into the 'green line' the user saw. Fixes: 'z' -> Vector3.BACK, _tilt_sign folded into joint AND sample lookup, weights_at() slices per-key 18-wide vectors, rebaked rig JSON (catalog hash updated). E2E check vs AnimationPlayer ground truth at +45deg: pos<1.1mm rot<0.08deg weights<0.005. Test now asserts twist-sign consistency, piston direction, and rigid-rod pin invariant.

Menu now has separate CouplerSelector + AttachmentSelector; tool items show supported coupler names. session tracks active_coupler_id/active_tool_id; attachment_changed emits composite 'coupler+tool' id.
